answer: A mechanism that actually bites: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because vault only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, relic is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any juniper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
